title: Adaptive pagination, deterministic typed responses, and unified error model for Embeddings SDKs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: Customers integrating high-volume embeddings pipelines have reported two classes of issues: (1) inefficient pagination leading to either very large single requests (OOMs or slow downstream processing) or tiny pages that increase round-trips and latency, and (2) inconsistent SDK surface across Python and TypeScript resulting in brittle error handling and type mismatches in typed environments. This ticket scopes a combined improvement: adaptive page sizing for embedding list/paginated endpoints, deterministic typed response contracts for both Python and TS clients (including streaming and resumable cursor support), and a unified error model that maps HTTP/transport/server errors to well-documented typed exceptions.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python + TypeScript) expose a stable EmbeddingsClient.list_embeddings(cursor?, page_size?) API with an 'adaptive_page_size' parameter that dynamically adjusts page_size based on observed latency and downstream processing throughput.

Typed response models (Python dataclasses/pydantic + TypeScript interfaces) are published for all list and streaming embedding responses; types are deterministic and documented so codegen and static checks succeed.

A unified error model is implemented: network/transport errors, transient server errors, quota/validation errors, and partial success (some items failed) are represented as distinct typed exceptions and error wrappers in both SDKs.
Backward-compatibility: existing call patterns without 'adaptive_page_size' behave identically to current SDKs (default page_size remains unchanged), and a migration guide is available.
Integration tests that simulate high-throughput ingestion and slow downstream consumers demonstrate improved end-to-end latency and fewer out-of-memory or retry storms.
Telemetry: new metrics emitted for page_size adjustments, per-request latency, cache/hit stats, and error categories; dashboards updated in Console to show adaptive pagination behavior.
Documentation: API docs, migration guide, and changelog entries completed prior to release.
Rollout: feature flag gated; gradual rollout to "hosted" customers with canary traffic before 100% release; smoke checks and rollback thresholds defined.
Types: TypeScript package passes 'npm run build' and unit tests; Python package passes lint, mypy checks, and unit tests in CI.
tasks: Design adaptive_page_size heuristic (initial proposal: start from requested page_size or 256 tokens, measure 95th-percentile latency; if latency < target and downstream throughput high, double page_size; if latency > target, halve page_size; clamp to min/max).
Define typed response schema for list and streaming endpoints (fields: id, vector, metadata, cursor, partial_failures).
Implement unified error classes: EmbeddingAPIError(base), EmbeddingTransientError, EmbeddingValidationError, EmbeddingQuotaError, EmbeddingPartialResultError.
Add server-side support for 'suggested_page_size' in list responses (optional) to help clients adapt more quickly.
Implement client-side adaptive controller with pluggable policy and a simple default policy that follows the heuristic above.
Add pagination helper utilities: resilient_cursor(), async iterator helpers for TS and Python, and a 'batch_and_emit' helper for common ingestion patterns.
Add comprehensive unit and integration tests including fault injection for partial failures and simulated high-latency downstreams.
Update SDK docs and migration guide; include code examples for both Python and TS.
Create Console dashboard tiles and alerts for adaptive pagination metrics.
Coordinate rollout with backend team: server change to include optional 'suggested_page_size' and annotate responses with 'partial_failures' when applicable.
Prepare feature-flag rollout plan and rollback criteria.

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Adaptive growth could cause memory OOMs in small foot-print clients. Mitigation: conservative default upper bound, and opt-out flag 'adaptive_page_size=false'.

Risk: New typed responses may break downstream customers using loose parsing. Mitigation: maintain backward-compatible JSON keys and provide a compatibility mode that returns legacy shapes for one release cycle.
Risk: Increased server CPU from recommended larger pages. Mitigation: server suggested_page_size logic will be conservative and we will monitor throughput metrics under canary traffic.
test_plan: Unit tests for controller behavior around growth/shrink policy.
Integration tests against canary backend with simulated slow consumer (delay consumer ack).
Fault-injection tests for partial failures and network timeouts.
Performance tests measuring throughput and per-item latency with and without adaptive pagination.
End-to-end smoke for both Python and TS SDK packaging and CI gates.
